sources.situation: the dev confirmed `stack.md` by hand, or a run is resumed. Someone runs `nio onboard start --empty` again, which is allowed from `in progress`, `skipped` and `done`. The code writes every doc in `DOCS`, all six rather than only `stack`, `architecture` and `infra`. It writes them unconditionally, so confirmed docs become `NEEDS CLARIFICATION` stubs with no backup and no message. `products.md` and `personas.md` are lost too. The spec said to write them only when they don't exist.

`.nio/project/stack.md` already holds confirmed content and the dev runs `start --empty`. The code overwrites it with blank sections, which is data loss. It does this for all six DOCS, including `product`, `personas` and `principles`, which FR-12 says are still grilled. The generated sections come from the invented `SECTIONS` map, not the CT-12 `HEADINGS`.

a repo that is in progress with stack.md already confirmed. `nio onboard start --empty` rewrites every one of the six docs with NEEDS CLARIFICATION. The write has no exists check, and the table's in-progress row says start is ignored there. The code also writes product, personas and principles, which CT-4 leaves out. The stack.md it writes has `## Frameworks` where CT-12 names `Dependencies` and `Commands`, so the template check fails when the doc is confirmed.

findings.reason: onboard.py line 93-94 loops over all six DOCS and calls write_text with no exists check. CT-4 and FR-12 limit this to stack, architecture and infra, and only when they don't exist.

sources.situation: onboarding is `done`. `nio onboard start` takes the `st["state"] = "in progress"` branch, which has no `done` check. Done is reopened and `--empty` overwrites docs (F1). `nio onboard skip x` sets `skipped` and loses `done`, so `seen` and the freshness baseline become meaningless. `start` on `in progress` also does not print `ignored`. The test `test_empty_start_writes_blank_docs` and the others never hit the `done` row.

onboarding is `done` and the dev runs `nio onboard skip "x"`. The code sets the state to `skipped` and prints `skipped`. CT-4 requires exit 1 with `onboarding is done already`. A completed onboarding is lost, and `nio status` then reports `skipped`. Skip on `skipped` is also not an `ignored: onboarding is skipped` no-op.

`act` runs `(d / f"{n}.md").write_text(...)` for all six DOCS with no existence check. A dev who has confirmed `stack.md` and `infra.md` runs `nio onboard start --empty`, or is on a repo that already has `.nio/project/` docs. The files are replaced with blank templates and the confirmed content is lost. This also writes `product`, `personas` and `principles`, which the contract does not list, and the same overwrite happens on a start after `skipped`. Nothing backs up the files, and FR-29 says a backup copy is made before NIO changes a file.

sources.situation: `pause` from `not started`, `done` or `skipped` sets `paused` (`st["state"] = "paused"`). A finished or deliberately skipped project then blocks every full and epic spec, because `spec.new` refuses `paused`. The CT-4 `ignore` cells should have printed `ignored` and changed nothing. `confirm` from `not started`, `skipped` or `done` adds to `confirmed` without changing state. A `confirm` from `done` can mutate the saved set after the freshness baseline was taken.

`pause` on `done` or `not started` sets the state to `paused`; `pause` on `done` reopens a finished onboarding and then blocks specs. `confirm` on `not started` records a doc as confirmed. `confirm` never checks that the doc file exists or passes the check_doc test, and never moves the state to `done` or saves `seen`. It prints `done` while the state stays `in progress`, so `spec.new` still refuses. `test_empty_start_writes_blank_docs` asserts `confirm stack` exits 1 in `paused`, which contradicts the ignore cell, so the test locks in the defect.

sources.situation: an agent or dev runs `nio onboard confirm infra` with no `infra.md`. It is recorded as confirmed with no check, and `NEEDS CLARIFICATION` stubs can be confirmed too. A later `@nio:onboard` resume then skips the doc, so a never-written doc counts as onboarded and agents' packs lack it. With `--empty` the state is never moved to `done`: `rest` always lists all six docs. `done` is also never saved, and `seen` is never saved. `--app` is not accepted at all, so unknown flags give an argparse usage error.

with `done` stored, `start` sets `in progress` again, `skip` sets `skipped`, and `pause` sets `paused`. Each one silently erases the finished onboarding and the reconcile path. `pause` on `not started` or `skipped` flips the state. `confirm` on `not started` or `skipped` records a doc and only prints `next:`. `confirm` also never checks that the doc file exists or passes CT-12, so an unwritten doc can be confirmed. `start` on `paused` raises "onboarding is paused", though CT-4 says a later start from `paused` resumes and keeps the saved `confirmed`. Only `pause` on `paused` follows the table.

CT-4 says confirm outside `in progress` is ignored. It also says confirm needs the doc file to exist and pass `check_doc`. The code confirms any doc in any state except paused, even `not started`, `skipped` or `done`. It never moves the state to `done` when the last doc is confirmed, and it saves no `seen`. Without those two steps nothing ever reaches `done`, so a full or epic spec stays refused after a complete onboarding. The code also does not write the progress file atomically (`f.write_text`), as CT-3 specifies.

findings.reason: Confirm (lines 97-102) only checks `doc in DOCS`, never the file or CT-12. `rest` walks all six DOCS, so `--empty` never ends in `done`. `done` is never saved. cli.py passes no `--app`.

sources.situation: `f.write_text(json.dumps(st))` truncates the file in place. A crash, a kill or two concurrent `confirm` runs leave torn JSON. Two parallel runs also lose one update (read, modify, write). Afterwards `spec.new` and `act` refuse with a clear message, but `nio status` calls `status_lines` outside any `try`. `progress` raises `ValueError`, so the whole status, including the index lines, ends in a traceback. Valid JSON of the wrong shape (`[]`, or a missing key like `confirmed`) raises an uncaught `TypeError` or `KeyError` in all paths. A skip reason containing a newline can also forge extra lines in `nio status` output.

A `pause` on a skipped project turns it into `paused`, so `spec.new` refuses again and the skip is lost. A `pause` on `done` demotes it to `paused`. A second `skip` replaces the stored reason. A `pause` on `not started` also changes it to `paused`. Unlike the paused-twice case, the tests never cover these.

onboarding is `done`. `nio onboard skip "x"` takes the skip branch, which sets `st.update(state="skipped", ...)` and saves, so a finished run becomes `skipped`. CT-4 says skip on `done` must exit 1 with `onboarding is done already`. `nio onboard start` on `done` skips the paused check and sets `"in progress"` again, so a run that "runs once" is reopened, where CT-4 says reject. findings.reason: The finding's situation text is empty, but the code supports it. `act` raises "onboarding is paused" for any `start` or `confirm` while paused, so a paused onboarding has no way back, where CT-4 says a later start from `paused` resumes. `start` and `skip` have no check for `done`: they overwrite the state, where CT-4 says exit 1. `start` on `in progress` and `skip` on `skipped` are not turned into `ignored:` either.
